banks.detail: October priced as a hold at ~84-85% (CME FedWatch 84%; Kalshi 87.5%, Oct 20) into the Oct 17-29 blackout — Warsh's last word was 'I don't prejudge meetings.' December hike now 88-90% (CME FedWatch Oct 20), up from the stale 70.3% Oct-12 read; range tight. 10Y 5.11% Tuesday (from 5.14% Monday; FRED DGS10 Oct 19 5.15%); 2Y ~4.78% (FRED DGS2 Oct 19 4.77%). The housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales -7.3% record low, ADP 18.5K) vs the hot inflation week (import prices +8.1% y/y).
banks.summary: The Fed is expected to hold in October, then decide on a hike in December. Recent inflation has run hot, which keeps the dollar supported while markets wait.

banks.detail: October-28 hike ~85-87%: LSEG via Reuters Oct 20 puts the chance at ~85%; CORRA OIS 87% with +22bp implied (bluegamma, Oct 20) — up from ~30% Friday on Macklem's Oct-17 IMF remarks (inflation forecast to be revised 'substantially higher' on energy). The Reuters Oct-19 '78% hold-bet' read is superseded — conflict resolved to the hike side. USD/CAD 1.405 (-0.42% Tuesday, Alberta referendum + crude bid). BMO/RBC/Desjardins all flipped to hike calls.
banks.summary: A weak jobs report made an October hike less likely, so the Bank of Canada is waiting on today's inflation numbers. A hot reading would put a hike back on the table and help the loonie.

banks.detail: October-29 hold ~97-98% (UBS Oct 20: only 2-3bp of an October move priced). December hike 84% (CaixaBank Research Oct 20). German PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%); EZ final CPI 3.8% confirmed. French revenue-section vote postponed to Oct 27 (formal vote Nov 3); OAT-Bund ~146bp. Lagarde: the fix 'lies at home in France.'
banks.summary: The ECB is expected to hold in October and is leaning toward a hike in December, because inflation is at a three-year high. France's budget trouble is the main thing weighing on the euro.

banks.detail: October 29-30 a hold at ~94%+ — Reuters Oct 20 (four BoJ sources): 'virtually no chance' of an October hike; the bank may upgrade its inflation forecast and hold steady. December hike ~73% (Reuters Oct 20). Ueda's 'quite close' to 2% leans December, not October. Japan's 20Y JGB auction saw strongest demand on record. Japan trade balance tonight 6:50pm CT. USD/JPY 158.04 (+0.29%).
banks.summary: The BoJ keeps signalling that more rate hikes are coming, probably in December rather than October. Higher Japanese rates would narrow the gap with the US and support the yen.

banks.detail: November 2-3 hike ~30%; December ~56%. Kent's 'restrictive enough?' line stands; Hauser speaks tonight 5:30pm CT (RBA Citi conference). AUD/USD 0.7002 (+0.32%). Q3 CPI Oct 28 the pivot. China LPR held for the 17th straight month (1y 3.00%, 5y 3.50%).
banks.summary: The RBA's tone has turned more hawkish, hinting rates may not be high enough yet. A hike in November is possible but not expected, and next week's inflation number is the key test.

banks.detail: November-5 hike ~95% to 4.00% (swaps/SONIA 95%; centralbank.watch 95.1%; Reuters: money markets 'almost fully priced'). UK labor beat sealed it: unemp 4.7% vs 4.9% fcst (lowest since mid-2025), wages 3.7%. Greene hawkish: wage disinflation 'has stalled at levels above those consistent with inflation at 2%.' Gilt auction solid: £4.3B at 5.418%, cover 3.61x. GBP/USD 1.339 (+0.66%). UK CPI Wednesday 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%).
banks.summary: The Bank of England is almost certain to raise rates on November 5, and the debate is already about December. This week's UK jobs and inflation data will shape how far it goes.
